name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
eligibility: HS seniors; GPA 3.0+; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; leadership + service
notes: 150 scholars selected nationally. One of the most prestigious HS scholarships.

name: Elks National Foundation Most Valuable Student
eligibility: HS seniors; U.S. citizens; scholarship, leadership, financial need
notes: 500 scholarships nationally at multiple award levels.

name: Caroline D. Bradley Scholarship
eligibility: Exceptional 7th graders; IQ or achievement testing required; any U.S. student
notes: One of the most prestigious merit scholarships for 7th graders. Apply in fall of 7th grade.

name: Coolidge Scholarship
eligibility: HS Juniors; any field; nominated through school or self-nominated
notes: Full ride; one of the most selective merit scholarships in the U.S.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
eligibility: Under 18; significant original work in STEM, arts, humanities, music, literature, or philosophy
notes: For profoundly gifted students. Three award levels.

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
eligibility: HS Juniors who take PSAT/NMSQT; semifinalists → finalists → scholars
deadline: Oct PSAT → Feb semifinalist → Apr scholar
notes: Taking the PSAT in 11th grade is the entry. Corporate/college awards often larger.

name: Presidential Scholars Program
eligibility: Automatic consideration via SAT/ACT scores; also arts and CTE categories; U.S. citizens
notes: Highest honor given to graduating HS seniors by the U.S. Dept. of Education. ~161/year.

name: AIAA Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: HS seniors and undergrads pursuing aerospace engineering or related; GPA 3.0+
notes: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics.

name: National Society of the Daughters of the American Revolution Essay Contest
eligibility: Grades 5-8 (American History Essay); HS (Christopher Columbus, etc.); U.S. students
notes: Multiple essay contests at different grade levels; accessible via local chapters.

name: Bank of America Scholarships
eligibility: HS seniors; multiple programs incl. Bank of America Student Leaders (paid internship + scholarship)
notes: Student Leaders: paid internship + Washington DC summit for 11th graders.

name: Wells Fargo Scholarship Program
eligibility: HS seniors; financial need + academic achievement + community involvement
notes: Need-based component; strong community-involvement focus.

name: Gates Scholarship
eligibility: African American, American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian/Pacific Islander American, or Hispanic; HS seniors; GPA 3.3+; financial need
notes: Full scholarship covering all college expenses. Very selective.

name: AI for Good Scholarship
eligibility: HS and undergrad students working on AI projects with social impact; multiple sponsors
notes: Multiple organizations run AI-for-good scholarships.

name: American Astronomical Society Scholarships
eligibility: HS and undergrad students interested in astronomy; multiple award tracks
notes: AAS funds astronomy-focused awards and research programs for pre-college students.

name: FBLA National Business Plan Competition
eligibility: HS students in FBLA chapters; business plan, entrepreneurship, finance events
notes: Future Business Leaders of America. Very active HS program nationally.

name: DECA Scholarships
eligibility: HS and college students in DECA; competitive events in entrepreneurship, marketing, finance, hospitality
notes: DECA competitive events are the entry point; scholarships to event winners.

name: Imagine America Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: HS seniors planning to attend a career college or technical school
notes: Specifically for students pursuing career/technical college paths.

name: U.S. Senate Youth Program (USSYP)
eligibility: HS Juniors (11th grade); two selected per state; must hold elected student office
notes: Washington Week in DC + $10,000 scholarship. Highly competitive.

name: Congressional App Challenge
amount: Winner displayed in U.S. Capitol + recognition
eligibility: Middle and HS students in any U.S. congressional district; any language; solo or team
notes: Winners' apps shown at the U.S. Capitol. Annual theme prompt.

name: USACO (USA Computing Olympiad)
amount: Recognition + college signal; top students represent USA at IOI
eligibility: Any K-12 student; online, four divisions (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum)
notes: Pathway: USACO Platinum → US team at IOI. Free.

name: Adobe Research Women-in-Technology Scholarship
eligibility: Female-identifying students studying CS, CE, digital media, or related; HS seniors and undergrads
notes: Also includes Adobe mentorship.

name: Microsoft Scholarship Program
eligibility: Students studying CS, engineering, or related; underserved community or diverse background
notes: Also offers paid internships.

name: Google Generation Scholarship
eligibility: Current HS seniors or undergrad/graduate students studying CS or related; various tracks
notes: Multiple tracks: Generation, Women in Tech, Hispanic, Black Scholars, etc.

name: NSPE Educational Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: HS seniors and undergrads; planning engineering degree
notes: National Society of Professional Engineers; multiple award tracks.

name: Engineers Without Borders Scholarship
eligibility: Engineering students committed to international humanitarian work

name: DiscoverE Future City Engineering Competition
eligibility: Grades 6-8 teams; design and build a model future city with a STEM sustainability theme
notes: $7,500 scholarship to 1st-place regional winner.

name: Society of Women Engineers (SWE) Scholarship
eligibility: Students who identify as women; enrolled or planning enrollment in engineering or tech
notes: Multiple scholarship tracks. Very accessible application.

name: Diamond Challenge — University of Delaware
eligibility: HS students worldwide; develop a high-growth venture concept; solo or team
notes: One of the most prestigious HS entrepreneurship competitions.

name: Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship (NFTE) Competition
eligibility: HS students from under-resourced communities; business plan + pitch
notes: NFTE Global Young Entrepreneur of the Year — national exposure + funding.

name: National History Day Competition
eligibility: Grades 6-12; historical research project in documentary, website, exhibit, performance, or paper format
deadline: Regional Feb-Mar; State Apr; Nationals June (DC)
notes: Strong NorCal regional presence. Nationals at University of Maryland.

name: Concord Review — Student History Journal
eligibility: HS students worldwide; rigorous historical research paper (avg 8,000 words)
notes: Most prestigious HS history journal in the U.S. Acceptance rate ~10%.

name: Association of Indians in America (AIA) Scholarship
eligibility: Students of Indian descent; academic excellence + community service
notes: One of the oldest Indian American organizations.

name: Indiaspora Scholarship
eligibility: Indian-origin students demonstrating exceptional leadership and academic excellence
notes: Focus on students of Indian origin with demonstrated impact.

name: Conrad Challenge
eligibility: HS students worldwide; teams develop innovations addressing global challenges in 4 categories
notes: NASA-affiliated; 4 challenge categories.

name: We the Future Contest — iCivics
eligibility: Middle and HS students; video, essay, or art on civic themes
notes: Accessible civics competition; multiple entry formats.

name: American Bar Association Law Day Essay Contest
eligibility: HS students; annual Law Day essay topic; sponsored by local bar associations
notes: Local bar associations feed into state/national.

name: Youth & Government Program — YMCA
eligibility: Grades 6-12; YMCA-affiliated; model state legislature and court programs
notes: Mock legislature, courts, and journalism. Strong pre-law foundation.

name: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
eligibility: HS students who have improved race relations in their communities
notes: Princeton University-sponsored.

name: MIT PRIMES
eligibility: HS students (grades 9-11); research with MIT faculty on math, CS, and science problems
notes: MIT PRIMES and PRIMES-USA (online). Free, no travel for the USA track.

name: MATHCOUNTS Competition Series
eligibility: Grades 6-8; chapter → state → national problem-solving math
deadline: Chapter Feb; State Mar; Nationals May
notes: $8,000 scholarship for national champion.

name: AMC / AIME / USAMO Pipeline
amount: USAMO winners receive medals and recognition
eligibility: Any K-12 student; AMC 8 (middle), AMC 10/12 (HS), then AIME, then USAMO/USAJMO
notes: Pathway to represent the USA at the IMO.

name: ASHRAE Scholarship
eligibility: Engineering students pursuing HVAC, refrigeration, or building systems engineering
notes: Am. Soc. of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers.

name: American Medical Association Foundation Scholarship
eligibility: Medical students and aspiring physicians; also pre-med programs for HS
notes: Pre-med HS students should look at AMA's pipeline programs.

name: John Locke Institute Essay Competition
eligibility: Under 19 (Senior); under 15 (Junior Prize); any country; essay in 10 subject categories
deadline: Register Feb 2 – Mar 31; submit by Jun 1
notes: 10 categories incl. Law, Philosophy, Politics. 63,000+ entries. Very prestigious.

name: Future of Science Award — Thermo Fisher
eligibility: Middle and HS students; original science research; accessible pathway
notes: Multiple Thermo Fisher-sponsored awards at ISEF and affiliated fairs.

name: JSHS — Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
eligibility: HS students with original STEM research; DoD-sponsored; regional heats → nationals
notes: DoD-sponsored. National finalist = significant recognition + scholarship.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI) — MIT
eligibility: Rising HS seniors worldwide; rigorous application; math/science research aptitude
notes: 6-week summer research program at MIT. ~80 spots globally.

name: Simons Foundation Research Fellowship
eligibility: HS students; research partnerships with university labs via Simons-affiliated programs
notes: Supports exceptional student researchers in math, physics, life sciences, CS.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
eligibility: HS seniors with original STEM research; independent or school-based
notes: Nation's oldest and most prestigious pre-college science competition.

name: Regeneron ISEF (International Science & Engineering Fair)
eligibility: HS students who qualify via an affiliated regional science fair (e.g., SVSEF)
deadline: Qualify via regional spring; ISEF Finals May
notes: World's largest international HS science fair. $9M+ total prizes.

name: Broadcom MASTERS
eligibility: Grades 6-8; qualify via an affiliated regional/state science fair
notes: Most prestigious national middle school science competition.

name: Regeneron ISEF Special Awards
eligibility: ISEF finalists; special awards from agencies and companies on top of category awards
notes: Special awards from NASA, USAF, NIH, NOAA, and 60+ organizations.
